title: CLCON/437/2020 of MANJU SHARMA Vs AMITA UPPRATI

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Contempt Petition No. 437 of 2020
Manju Sharma ...Petitioner
Vs.
Amita Upprati and Another ...Respondents
Advocate: Mrs. Neetu Singh, Advocate for the petitioner
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
The petitioner herein, is the second wife of late Mr. Arun
Kumar Sharma. The controversy pertaining to the settlement
and appointment of the service benefits was laid to rest by the
judgement of the Division Bench of this Court in a judgement,
which was rendered on 16.12.2017, whereby the Division Bench
of this Court, had disposed of the writ petition, as well as the
Special Appeal No. 648 of 2017, Smt. Manju Sharma Vs. State
of Uttarakhand and others, with the following directions:-
"6. When the matter came up, we referred the matter for mediation. The
parties have arrived at a settlement before the Mediator. The terms of the
settlement read as follows:
"1. That Late Mr. Arun Kumar Sharma husband of Smt.
Manju Sharma and Smt. Renu Sharma was working as a
pharmacist in the State Government and he died during his
service period Smt. Renu Sharma is the one son master Sidhant
Shamra aged about 6 years and a daughter Km. Sristi Sharma
aged about 4 years.
2. That Late Mr. Arun Kumar left two wife and three
children after his death some disputes relating to the family
pension pensionary benefits and appointment under the dying in
harness rules arrises between the parties so the appellant file the
said Special Appeal before this Hon 'ble High Court now in the
mediation both the parties are agree to settle their dispute in
mediation. According to the settlement the first wife Smt.
Renu Sharma will be entitled to received the family pension
and her daughter Km. Kirti Sharma will get her appointment
under the dying in harness rules and the children master
Sidhant Sharma and Km. Siristi Sharma through their
mother Smt. Manju Sharma will received total service
benefits (gratuity, leave encashment, group insurance, CPSN)
except family pension.
3. That the both the parties undertake to give respect and
honor to each other.

2
4. That the parties hereto confirm and declare that/hey have
voluntarily & out of their own free will arrived at this settlement
/agreement in the presence of their respective Advocates.
5. That the settlement has been read over & explained to the
parties in their own language in presence of their advocates.
Signature of parties are also identified by their Advocates.
6. That both the parties are bound by the terms & conditions
of this settlement agreement."
2. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that
subsequent to the judgement dated 06.12.2017, the respondent, had
in compliance of the directions given therein, particularly, that as
contained in sub para (2) of para 6 of the Division Bench's
judgement, certain amount has already been disbursed to her, which
the petitioner was otherwise entitled to receive; except that the CPSN
amount, which was payable towards the family pension.
3. She admits the fact in the present contempt petition, that in
compliance of the judgement of the Division Bench of this Court, the
respondent did disbursed a certain amount to her, as the same finds
reference in the pleadings raised in the contempt petition; but,
partially the same was not complied with.
4. When this matter was taken up at an admission stage, a query
was made from the petitioner's counsel to clarify as to on what date
the first payment was made and which according to the petitioner's
expectation was not a complete compliance of the judgement, and
the said query was made particularly in order to determine the cause
of action for her for the purposes of her filing the contempt petition,
in the light of the provisions contained under Section 20 of the
Contempt of Courts Act. Subsequent thereto, the Court passed yet
another order on 11.12.2020, and in compliance thereto, the
petitioner has filed a supplementary affidavit along with an
Interlocutory Application No. 12230/2020.

3
5. Today, when the contempt proceedings of hearing the
contempt revived and was being heard, the Court, yet again
reiterated the same query, as to when did the first payment was made
to her, because that would be the cut off, which would enable the
Court to determine the period of limitation as has been provided
under Section 20 of the Contempt of Courts Act, because as per the
opinion of this Court, the dissatisfaction of compliance would start
from the date of the partial compliance of payment of the amount
was made by the respondent.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn attention of
this Court to the representation made by the petitioner, on
29.05.2019, wherein, admittedly, as per her own showing, she has
pleaded that it was on 25.09.2018, the respondent had paid an
amount of Rs. 3,10,998/-. Meaning thereby, logically, if the
limitation is to be determined for the purposes of Section 20 of the
Contempt of Courts Act, it would be w.e.f. 25.09.2018 and not on
the basis of subsequent correspondences which were made by the
petitioner for compliance and payment of the balance payment,
which was not remitted to her. Rest of the communication or the
communication dated 31.08.2020, on which reliance has been
placed, alleging that there was tacit denial, imparting the knowledge
of a non-compliance to the petitioner of the Division Bench
judgement, may not be a foundation to determine the bar, which had
been created by Section 20 of the Contempt of Courts Act for
entertaining the contempt.
7. At the most, even if a lenient view is taken for the purposes of
determining the cut off of one year for filing of the contempt
petition, according to the correspondences of the petitioner herself
that would be from the order dated 25.09.2018, that has expired
much earlier and hence this Court cannot initiate the proceedings for

4
contempt for non-compliance of the judgement dated 06.12.2017
after the lapse of aforesaid period.
8. Consequently, the contempt petition lacks merit and the same
is accordingly dismissed being barred by Section 20 of the Contempt
of Courts Act of 1971.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 09.12.2020 Mahinder/
